identification: Five small British sterling spoons, all hallmarked (cloud scan's 'some plated' looks wrong: every handle back carries a hallmark set): (1) shell-bowl pierced sugar sifter spoon with cast rococo-scroll handle, Victorian/Edwardian, handle tip chipped/notched; (2) gilt-bowl scalloped jam/preserve spoon with twisted stem and pierced cast foliate terminal, British hallmarked (Birmingham/Chester type, c.1900-1920), not Continental; (3)-(4) a matching pair of fiddle-pattern salt spoons, engraved script initial, maker 'WH' (possibly with a preceding initial) beside a single strip-punch of four marks; (5) shell-bowl tea caddy spoon with bright-cut engraved handle and three small oval/cut-corner punches, a style typical of Birmingham c.1800-1840 caddy spoons (unconfirmed). Estimate A$40-70, current bid A$25.

viewing_check: Loupe each spoon: caddy spoon maker/date (Birmingham anchor + duty head = Georgian/William IV; known makers Joseph Taylor, Samuel Pemberton, Joseph Willmore would lift it to A$150-250); salt spoons town and date in the four-mark strip, maker WH; confirm the twist spoon is British not 800 Continental. Weigh the lot. Check the caddy shell bowl for splits and the sifter tip chip.
